title: Input-head orbit of the saving machine
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of the saving machine on $x$ with no work tapes. Suppose the machine is in state false and the input-head position is at most the length of $x$. For every natural number $r$ no greater than that position, after $r$ rounds—each consisting of one machine step—the state remains false, the input-head position is its initial position minus $r$, and the output is unchanged. After one more round than the initial input-head position, the state is true, the input-head position is zero, and the output is unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: The input $x$ is a list of Boolean symbols.
The configuration $c$ has zero work tapes and is for input $x$.
The input-head position is at most the length of $x$.
The round count $r$ is a natural number at most the initial input-head position.
